findings.title: Negative (and zero) litres are accepted and saved
findings.where: POST /api/waterings; Beds page 'Record past watering' form
findings.steps: On /beds open 'Record past watering', enter litres -5 and save (or POST {"bed_id":1,"watered_on":"2026-11-01","litres":-5}). Also try litres 0 or -1e300 via the API.
findings.expected: Amounts of zero or below are refused with a visible reason. The client says 'greater than zero' and the server answers 4xx.
findings.actual: The client only rejects exactly 0, so -5 passes. The server's litres field has le=10000 but no lower bound, so it returns 201 for -5, 0 and -1e300. Negative amounts then show on the dashboard and the waterings page and lower the page's total.
findings.evidence: API returned 201 {"id":3,...,"litres":-5.0}, 201 for litres 0.0 and 201 for litres -1e+300. beds.vue savePastWatering checks only `litres === 0`. schemas.py WateringIn has `Field(default=None, le=10_000)` with no gt=0.

findings.title: NaN litres causes a 500 Internal Server Error
Out-of-range bed_id causes a 500 error on the waterings endpoints
findings.steps: GET /api/waterings?bed_id=99999999999999999999, or POST {"bed_id":99999999999999999999}. You can also open /waterings?bed=99999999999999999999 in the web app.
findings.actual: 500 Internal Server Error, because SQLite overflows on an integer that is too large

findings.title: Waterings page and dashboard 'Recent waterings' error states have no retry
findings.steps: Make GET /api/waterings fail, e.g. stop the API or use a bad bed query, then load / or /waterings
findings.expected: An error message with a Retry button that refetches without a page reload
findings.actual: Only an AlertMessage is shown. index.vue does not even take `refresh` from the waterings fetch, and waterings.vue has no retry control.
findings.evidence: index.vue: `const { data: waterings, error: wateringsError } = wateringsResult`, and the template shows no retry button. waterings.vue shows the same with no retry button.

findings.title: Bed filter fails silently when the beds request fails
findings.steps: Make GET /api/beds fail while GET /api/waterings succeeds, then open /waterings
findings.expected: An error explaining that the bed list could not be loaded, with a retry
findings.actual: bedsResult.error is ignored. The filter dropdown shows only 'All beds' as if no beds existed, and a ?bed= value from a link has no matching option.
findings.evidence: waterings.vue: `const { data: beds } = bedsResult`. The error is never read.

findings.title: A retry after a timeout or network failure can record a watering twice
findings.steps: Click 'Water now' and let the response be lost (slow network), then click again
findings.actual: Each POST inserts a new row and there is no idempotency key, so a retry after an unseen success creates a duplicate. The client fetch also has no 10 s timeout, so the button can stay on 'Watering…' as long as the request hangs.
findings.evidence: waterings.py create_watering always INSERTs. useApiClient sets no timeout.

findings.title: 'Water now' date uses the server's local day while the time is UTC, and past dates are checked against the server's date
findings.steps: Use the app from a time zone that differs from the server's near midnight. Click 'Water now', or record a past watering dated 'today' in your own time zone.
findings.actual: watered_on comes from the server's local date while the display converts the UTC watered_at to the viewer's zone, so the date and time can disagree. Sorting uses watered_on. A watering dated with the client's todayIso() can be refused as 'in the future' when the server is behind.
findings.evidence: waterings.py: `now.astimezone().date()` combined with a UTC watered_at, and schemas.py compares against date.today()
